text:
```yaml
name: Regenerate Examples and Safety Checks

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up Rust
      uses: actions-rs/toolchain@v1
      with:
        toolchain: stable
        profile: minimal
        override: true

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        cargo install just
        just setup

    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        cargo test --workspace
        just test-db
        just test-e2e

    - name: Check code quality
      run: |
        cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
        cargo fmt -- --check
        cargo dupes

    - name: Generate examples and safety checks
      run: just generate-examples

    - name: Commit changes
      run: |
        git add tokf-filter/examples.rs tokf-common/safety/
        git commit -m "chore(tokf): regenerate examples and add safety checks"
        git push origin main

  publish-to-server:
    needs: build-and-test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up Rust
      uses: actions-rs/toolchain@v1
      with:
        toolchain: stable
        profile: minimal
        override: true

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        cargo install just
        just setup

    - name: Publish examples and safety data
      run: just publish-examples

    - name: Commit and push changes
      run: |
        git add tokf-server/src/main.rs tokf-server/migrations
        git commit -m "chore(tokf): publish updated examples and safety data"
        git push origin main
```

This GitHub Actions workflow file is designed to automate the process of regenerating examples and adding safety checks to the `mpecan/tokf` repository. It includes steps for building and testing the code, checking code quality, generating examples and safety checks, and publishing the updated data to the server. The workflow is triggered on pushes and pull requests to the `main` branch.
